policy: Each senior global tournament is calibrated on the real tournament-wide averages of the previous edition (the repository rule that a season is calibrated on the real averages of the one before it; AGENTS.md, Game engine, league environment policy). An edition may be read only on or after its publication_date. These describe the era's international style of play, not any team's results.
value_format: {value, status: sourced|unverified|derived, source, note?}. sourced = stated by the source; derived = computed here from sourced totals (method recorded); unverified = not established, value null.
units: Per team-game averages: every game counts twice (once per team). Games are 40 minutes (4 x 10) plus any overtime; no adjustment for overtime is made.
possessions_formula: FGA - ORB + TOV + 0.44 * FTA, per team-game

calibration_map.note: 2002_world_championship is recorded as the edition before 2004 (completeness; it calibrates no simulated tournament). Rule break: 2010 World Championship was played with the 6.25 m three-point line and trapezoid lane; the 2012 Olympics with 6.75 m and the rectangle (library/fiba/fiba_rules.json). Its three-point rates are a pre-change environment.

unresolved: 2002 World Championship: offensive and defensive rebounds, assists, steals, blocks, turnovers and personal fouls by team (and so possessions). archive.fiba.com is offline (TLS failure), web.archive.org refused connections, and the current FIBA history site publishes box scores for only 1 of 62 games.
2006 World Championship: ORB, DRB, AST, STL, BLK, TOV, PF are averages over the 51 of 80 games with a published official box score, not full-tournament totals.
2008 Olympics: the Basketball-Reference team row for China lists 434 points against 432 implied by its makes; listed points kept (difference 2 points over the tournament).
Turnover definitions across sources (Basketball-Reference international tables vs FIBA box scores) were not reconciled; team turnovers may be counted differently.
notes: Shooting totals for 2010 agree exactly between Basketball-Reference and FIBA (12,338 points; 4,353/9,727 FG; 1,321/3,729 3P; 2,311/3,255 FT).
Basketball-Reference's G column for the 2010 World Championship sums to 177 instead of 160 and was not used for the divisor.
